sentences.text: The issue involved in all the four Writ Petitions is pertaining to the question of acquisition of a property, over which, the petitioners are claiming title as title holders, whereas, the Government is maintaining a stand that the said property is vested with the Government.

is filed by the petitioners essentially with a prayer not to proceed with the acquisition or taking over possession of any portion of 6.80 ares of land, except in accordance with the procedure provided under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ('2013 Act', for short).

sentences.text: The second Writ Petition is W.P.(C) No.34499/2024 filed by the petitioners themselves seeking quashment of Exts.P23 and P24, which are reports of the revenue authorities, which recommends cancellation of mutation in favour of the petitioners.

The next Writ Petition is W.P.(C) No.42255/2024 is, again, one preferred by the petitioners, whereby the petitioners seek to quash Ext.P36, as per which, W.P.(C) Nos.23903, 34499, 42255 and 42895 of 2024 - 12 - 2025:KER:66471 the mutation in favour of the petitioners was cancelled, unilaterally according to the petitioners.
The fourth Writ Petition is W.P.(C) No.42895/2024 is also filed by the petitioners seeking to quash Ext.P38, which pertains to cancellation of mutation in favour of the petitioners.
2. This Court, by Order dated 21.08.2025, directed the respondent authorities to produce the documents in proof of adherence to the statutory provisions of 2013 Act.

Such an Order was passed in the light of the specific contention made by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the I.R. Bahuleyan & Co vs The District Collector on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61237815/

sentences.text: 3. Today, when the matter is taken up for consideration, learned counsel for the 7 th respondent would produce the notification under Sections 4 and 11 of the 2013 Act.

Having perused the same,
the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that their property does not find a place W.P.(C) Nos.23903, 34499, 42255 and 42895 of 2024 - 13 - 2025:KER:66471 in the said notifications.

In answer to the same, it is the contention of the learned Standing Counsel for the 7th respondent that the said property is not liable to be included in the notifications under Sections 4 and 11, inasmuch as the Government maintains that the property is vested with the Government and the petitioners have no title to the same.
4. This Court is of the opinion that the issue with respect to title, in respect of the property sought to be acquired, cannot be agitated in a proceeding under Article 226 of the Constitution.
The petitioners have to approach the statutory authority as per the scheme of 2013 Act.

In adopting that course, it was pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioners that, since the petitioners'
property does not find a place in Sections 4 and 11 notifications, the statutory remedy as per the scheme of the Act is not available with the petitioner.
That, of course, is a situation which can be remedied under Article 226 of the Constitution.

. Learned counsel for the 7th respondent would submit that the Award amount in respect of 2.78 ares, out of 6.80 ares, can be deposited and if the claim of the petitioners is ultimately found to be maintainable, the same can be disbursed to the petitioners, together with their rights to seek enhancement, whatsoever.
It was emphasised by the learned counsel for the 7th respondent that because of the interim order passed by this Court in these Writ Petitions, the acquisition proceedings have been stalled.

6. In the circumstances, there will be a direction to the 7th respondent to deposit the amount corresponding to 2.78 ares before the reference court in terms of Section 64 of the 2013 Act, which is the District Court, Ernakulam.
Upon effecting such deposit, the District Court will take immediate steps to deposit the same in a nationalised bank, so that the interest component is not lost to the ultimate beneficiary.

Further,
this Court recognise the petitioners' right to proceed under Section 64 of the 2013 Act to establish their right over the property before the District W.P.(C) Nos.23903, 34499, 42255 and 42895 of 2024 I.R.
